claim: When a spawn passes through a shell, assert the child's OBSERVED argv carries the restriction rather than the vector you built - a zero-length argument is deleted by concatenation, and the flag it belonged to then consumes the next flag as its value, silently removing a declared permission stance with no error anywhere.
because: Measured on win32 where the CLI is a .cmd shim needing shell:true: --allowed-tools "" --max-turns 1 reached the child as --allowed-tools=--max-turns plus a stray positional, so both the tool allowlist and the turn cap were absent on the only platform the app runs on, while the source comment described a sandbox. No in-process assertion could see it - the loss happens after the array stops existing.

claim: When classifying a dependency's failure, order the signals: what the dependency STATED outright (status code, structured field) decides first, and a text heuristic over its prose is the last resort reached only when the stated signals are silent - a heuristic evaluated first will overrule the code, and it will do so on ordinary vocabulary rather than on exotic input.
because: Measured: an adapter computed refusal = status===451 || /moderat|policy|not allowed|prohibited/i.test(body) and threw on it before checking 429/401/403. 'policy' is ordinary throttling and auth vocabulary, so a 429 reading 'quota policy exceeded' was classified as the model declining the brief - and in this taxonomy a refusal is never retried while a throttle always is, so the two are opposites. Three of six probe cases flipped. taxonomy-design already states 'the stated interval always wins' for retry intervals; the same precedence is not stated for the classification itself.

claim: When a closed vocabulary needs an ORDER, hold it as a total map from the vocabulary type (Record<Kind, rank>) rather than as an array of that type - an array type-checks its entries and never its completeness, and the lookup that follows (indexOf) answers a missing member with a value that is not 'unknown' but 'first'.
because: Measured: SPINE_ORDER was readonly MovementRole[] and spineSort used indexOf, so a role absent from the list ranked -1 and led the composed trailer. A probe composing an unranked role produced 'button -> cold-open -> climax'. Converting to Record<MovementRole, number> makes the omission a build error and the derived order cannot disagree with the rank. The failure is invisible precisely because the compiler IS checking the declaration - just not the property that matters.

claim: A URL that arrives inside a DEPENDENCY'S RESPONSE is attacker-controlled input to your server, not a trusted address: validate scheme, IP literals and resolved addresses before fetching it, and re-validate every redirect hop with redirect:manual - a pre-flight check on the first hop alone is defeated by a legitimate host answering 302 to a private address.
because: Measured twice in this fleet on the same shape. Here: an image downloader bounded response SIZE and TIMEOUT for a URL its own comment described as 'a URL a model handed us', and never checked where it pointed; a plate URL naming the cloud metadata endpoint was fetched and returned to the caller as base64. In a sibling app the identical class was found where the first hop WAS checked and the redirects were not. The two bounds that were present are the ones a reviewer thinks of; the destination is the one that carries the credential.

claim: A gate whose POPULATION is a hand-written list can only ever describe the codebase on the day it was typed: derive the set it walks from the filesystem or the schema, exempt members one at a time with a stated reason, and assert the walk found something before trusting its clean verdict - otherwise the gate reads the implementation's own list and reports 'all covered' about the four things it knows.
because: Measured twice in one repository. An auth probe written to catch an unauthenticated spending route enumerated four handlers by hand; five routes arrived afterwards, one of them ungated and spawning an 800-second paid run, and the probe could not see it. A bundle gate's server-only variable list carried the comment 'kept in step with .env.example' and had drifted six names behind, including a live vendor credential. Both were fixed by deriving the population; both had been green throughout.

claim: When a spawned agent CLI is fed its prompt over stdin, attach an 'error' listener to the child's stdin stream: a stream failure is an EVENT, not a throw at the call site and not something child.on('error') reports - that one covers the SPAWN, not the pipe - and an unhandled 'error' event is re-raised by Node as an uncaughtException that ends the host process instead of the call.
because: Measured 2026-08-29 on Windows, where the spawn must go through shell:true because the binary is a .cmd shim. With the binary absent, cmd starts, exits, and the 2MB prompt lands on a closed pipe: 'Error: write EOF', uncaught, process gone. The transport had a carefully written not-installed verdict and a router above it whose whole promise is a fallback ladder - and neither could ever run, because nothing survived long enough to classify anything. The absence of the binary is exactly the case the ladder exists for, so this defect is invisible on every machine that has it installed and total on every machine that does not.

claim: A gate that detects compliance by MATCHING THE NAME of a chokepoint must enumerate every door into that chokepoint and assert each name still resolves at its source - a chokepoint grows siblings (a variant wrapper for a surface the first one does not fit), and a single-name matcher then reports compliant code as violating, which is the failure that kills a gate rather than the one that embarrasses it.
because: Deriving the POPULATION from the filesystem - the fix this repo already applied to the same probe - did not save it. lib/apiAuth.ts grew two more doors after the matcher was written (an access-check without the money rate bucket, for a surface that legitimately bursts; and the raw verdict, for a route serving an that cannot carry an Authorization header). Nine committed, genuinely gated routes read as UNGATED and the blocking suite was red on main. A gate red for a false reason stops refusing anything: everyone learns to step over the failure, and the next actually-ungated route lands inside it. The repair is a door TABLE plus an assertion that each door is still exported - so a renamed door reddens the gate loudly instead of silently reclassifying the codebase.

claim: When a model is asked for a value from a CLOSED vocabulary and the schema is not natively enforced, a value outside the set is UNMEASURED, not a mismatch: drop the field from both sides of the score rather than crediting it zero - because the same number almost always gates a retry loop or a selection, so scoring unknown as wrong spends real money chasing a field nobody read.
because: Measured on a style-extraction engine. `styleScore` compared a vision readback against a target with `===` and scored anything else 0; a readback agreeing on every field but drifting on ONE scored 0.900 instead of 1.000 over the nine weights actually readable. That number is compared against the loop's target (0.85) and is what picks the recipe a style ships with, so the drift bought another generation round AND could change the winning recipe. The same codebase already refused off-vocabulary values at the synthesis door and already returned null rather than zero for a missing readback - the collapse survived only in the one function whose output was load-bearing, which is the pattern: the honest handling gets written where it is cheap and forgotten where it decides.

claim: Write-temp-then-rename is only half of an atomic write on Windows: os.replace/MoveFileEx raises PermissionError while any other handle to the DESTINATION is open, so on a file something polls - the exact case the pattern is reached for - the bare rename converts a torn read into a failed write. Retry the rename briefly and re-raise if it will not settle.
because: Measured on a 30 KB JSON index that a page polls and a CLI appends to. The plain write lost 38 of 50 reads to unparseable content. Swapping it for write-temp-then-rename took torn reads to zero and lost 32 of 40 WRITES - a different defect wearing the fix's clothes, and one that would have shipped as an improvement on the strength of the pattern's reputation. With a short retry: 0 torn reads, 0 failed writes, and the residue is a PermissionError the READER sees (never ENOENT, so never a silently empty document). The sibling module in the same directory had carried the bare rename with a comment explaining that the page polls the file, so the exposure was already live in the path whose failure aborts an hours-long GPU run.

claim: A test runner's own defaults are part of the gate, and the focus primitive (.only / fit / fdescribe) is the one that turns a green suite into a green lie: it does not fail, it SHRINKS - so audit the runner config for it before writing another probe, because no test can catch it (under .only, the test that would have caught it is one of the tests that does not run).
because: Measured on a repo whose probe lane is a blocking CI job and a pre-push hook, and which already carried a probe named gate-vacuous-pass opening with 'a check that examined nothing must not count as enforcement'. Playwright's forbidOnly defaults to false and neither config set it; adding .only to one case took `npm test` from 317 passed to '1 passed', exit 0, green everywhere - the 316 probes guarding money routes, auth, SSRF and the identity wipe silently did not run. The team had internalised gate-liveness thoroughly enough to write a probe about a vacuous pass inside one function, and the same hole sat in the runner that ran it, one config line away, for the whole suite.

claim: When a long run's JOB record is persisted and its RESULT record is not, the job outlives the screen as a standing claim about results that no longer exist - so either give the result the job's lifetime or make the surface reconcile the two out loud. The reload correction ('interrupted') fires only on a job still RUNNING, so a job that already SETTLED is never corrected, and the settled one is therefore the only one that can lie.
because: Measured on a follow-up research queue whose record was deliberately lifted above the component tree so navigation could not lose it, beside a job store persisted to localStorage. The subject's own technique already says 'the job record is the truth, and it outlives the screen', and warns about the inverse failure - a run living only in component state, whose result 'lands nowhere'. This is that failure turned around and it is the one that ships: after a reload the bell read 'done - Results are staged against the notebook' and the queue it pointed at was empty, with nothing on either side accounting for the difference. The module's own header asserted the case was already covered because lib/jobs writes 'interrupted' over a reload - true only of a RUNNING job, and a returned follow-up settles itself 'done' in the same tick it writes its results. A comment stating the guarantee was what stopped anyone looking.

claim: When sizing a LOCAL vendor row for MoE checkpoints, gate on NVMe bandwidth and RAM, not VRAM: expert-streaming engines (Colibri-class) run 321B-with-vision on a 25 GB-RAM floor, and the decode floor is bytes-touched-per-token divided by disk bandwidth (4.8 GB/token for GLM-5.3-Flash - approximately 24 s/token at 200 MB/s, approximately 1-3 s/token on PCIe-4 NVMe with a warm RAM cache).
because: Colibri v1.10.1 docs, measured reference numbers; local experiment on Wolf in progress - see librarian/sources/2026-09-01-colibri-glm53-experiment.md for the pre-registered protocol and decision rule.

claim: When comparing local MoE engines, classify by WHERE the expert tier ends: RAM-resident engines (FreeToken-class: offload/hybrid backends, PCIe-streamed misses, order-of-magnitude faster decode) cap at what host RAM holds, while NVMe-streaming engines (Colibri-class) extend the tier to disk and cap at disk bandwidth - on a 64GB-RAM box the two reach entirely different model classes (~120B vs 321B+), and 'runs 290B+ locally' claims are meaningless without the RAM assumption stated.
because: FreeToken docs/models.md (RAM-resident backends; 'Multimodal checkpoints are served text-only') vs Colibri glm53-flash.md (25GB RAM floor, 4.8GB/token disk touch); full comparison in librarian/sources/2026-09-01-colibri-glm53-experiment.md.

claim: When deciding whether a reference-governance rule can be measured on a given stack, ask what the RUNTIME does with the reference, not what the prompt says about it: an img2img denoise-window runner (Flux 2 via ComfyUI) admits the reference as a latent and has no labelled attachment channel, so reference-role-map/s ordering rule (the role declaration must LEAD the prompt, never trail it) has nothing to order there and is untestable on the local /usr/bin/bash lane; it is a claim about attachment-carrying multimodal stacks (Nano Banana, Gemini) and can only be closed on a billed one.
because: dojo cycle 2026-09-01-emblem-slot, phase 2/3: gravitone records a LIVE deviation on reference-role-map (lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:188-192 attaches a subject image plus up to 13 style references with no role declaration; on the generate path the label trails the prompt) but the deviation cannot be trained on the stack the cycle was pinned to. Not a verdict - no pairs were judged; the cycle failed on GPU contention.

claim: Keep two readback instruments per eye and never conflate them: a closed-enum schema for GRADING (comparable, arithmetic-safe, flattening by design) and a taught free-prose deep read for SEEING (roles, shapes, layers) - and when comparing models as eyes, hold the prompt constant, because a 321B-vs-27B class gap can be pure elicitation (measured: a taught prompt closed it at 25s/$0 on the 27B).

claim: When a child is spawned through `shell: true` on Windows, a timeout must kill the tree from the LIVE shell pid (`taskkill /pid <shell> /T /F`) before any plain signal, because `child.kill()` ends cmd.exe alone, the grandchild keeps running and holds the inherited pipes so `close` never fires, and once the shell is gone the tree can no longer be walked from it.
because: Measured 2026-09-05 with the engine's exact spawn shape: after child.kill() shell dead / grandchild alive; taskkill /T on the live shell pid ended both in under a second; taskkill on the dead shell pid found nothing. Landed as lib/claudeCli.ts#killTree with a real-process probe and a negative control.

claim: When a shell resolves the command name for you, detect a missing binary from the shell's own stderr sentence ('is not recognized as an internal or external command', 'command not found'), not from the documented exit code, because cmd.exe under Node's shell spawn exits 1 rather than the 9009 an interactive prompt reports, and a classifier written from the docs is green against the wrong number while the real case stays misclassified.
because: Measured 2026-09-05: spawn('definitely-not-a-binary', {shell:true}) -> code 1, stderr the sentence. The first cut of the fix keyed on 9009 and would have missed every real Windows case; the transport probe flipped from `failed` to `not-installed` only once the sentence was the primary signal.

claim: When an aria-live region is driven by framework state (React setState), put the clear and the write in separate tasks, because two state writes in one task batch into one commit, the clear never reaches the DOM, and an utterance whose text equals the previous one produces no mutation and is never voiced.
because: Found in a queue that deliberately wrote '' then text 'so a repeat is not swallowed' - the sink was React state and the repeat was exactly what was swallowed (two plates with one name removed in a row voice once). Fixed by scheduling the write one tick after the clear; the queue probe pins the two-tick contract.

claim: When a repo's gate suite covers one language and its build contains another, write that second language's FIRST check to a stdlib-only constraint, because a check that needs a dependency install is input-nondeterministic and can therefore only ever be advisory -- which is the reason it stays unwritten.
because: gravitone-gcloud's CI installs Node and nothing else; both test lanes are TypeScript, and 965 lines of Python that run for hours on a GPU and then write a verdict were executed by no gate at all. Every gate was green and every gate was honest -- gate-liveness does not cover this, because the gate never existed to die. A 200-line stdlib-only selftest (verified green with PIL, numpy, requests, httpx, cv2 and torch blocked at import) found 3 real defects on its first run, two of them falsifying the README's two headline promises; being stdlib-only is what lets a CI job run it with no pip step and still block under this repo's own blocking-by-input-determinism doctrine.

claim: When a derived check accepts a cleanup/restore hook by its PRESENCE, require the hook body to touch the resource the check is about, because a hook that restores something else satisfies a presence test and the leak it was written to catch stays invisible.
because: env-isolation.probe.spec.ts accepted any test.afterEach( as an env restore; music-failure-classification's afterEach restores fetch only and its beforeEach sets ELEVENLABS_API_KEY - witnessed as 'probe-key' in every later file with the check reporting 0 offenders. Fixed dbd5b9a by reading the afterEach body.

claim: When you remove a duplicated condition by extracting it into a shared predicate, assert BOTH the predicate's behaviour AND the call site's adoption of it, because a test that drives the predicate stays green when a call site reverts to its own copy â€” the extraction is what you fixed, the adoption is what you shipped.
because: Extracting a notebook section's render condition into sectionRenders() and driving it from a probe: reverting the component to map the unfiltered list left all five assertions green. Only seeding the component revealed it; the probe now reads the call site too (e28b972).

claim: A compositor that gates its TEXT layer on a fact citation will gate its ELEMENT layer on nothing, in the same validator, unless the technique says elements are figures too - so causal-arrow-discipline's 'an arrow is a figure whose value is because' needs to be a schema requirement on the element record, not a direction-time review step.

This is a repo that took the subject seriously enough to make the grade travel (a55dc9f) and still shipped the asymmetry, which suggests the failure is in where the technique puts the obligation.

claim: negative-prompting should require the delivery CHANNEL be declared on the provider and stamped into the output's provenance, not merely adapted per vendor, because a side-by-side comparison otherwise reads a native-field-versus-prose-clause difference as a model difference.

claim: style-first-token-ordering treats an unusual aspect ratio as a prompt-POSITION problem; the stronger move is to take the format out of the prompt entirely - a required typed field with no default, carried as an API parameter no encoder window can truncate - with prompt-position as the fallback for vendors that have no such field.

claim: When an offline-conversion upload pipeline sets its window or its alarm, take the window from the platform's current import guidelines per conversion type and not from one generic number, because the platform's standard window is longer (90 days after the last click) than the 63 days the registry states, and 63 days applies only to one conversion type.
